name: Unmei Tarot
tagline: Web app that deals a tarot spread and has an AI write the interpretation.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanic here is a shuffle, a spread layout, and a prompt. The 78-card Rider-Waite-Smith deck is public domain, the card meanings are in every LLM's training data, and the reading itself is one API call with the drawn cards and the user's question stuffed into context. An agent can produce a working local version with card art, reversals, three or four spread types, and saved reading history in one sitting. What you will not reproduce for free is the mood: the art direction, the animation of the flip, the pacing that makes the whole thing feel like a ritual rather than a JSON response.
coreLoopDIY: Shuffles a 78-card deck, deals a chosen spread with reversals, and sends the positions plus your question to an LLM that writes the reading.
requirements: An OpenAI or Anthropic API key, a few cents per reading
Public domain Rider-Waite-Smith card scans, downloadable from Wikimedia Commons
Node 20 and a browser; no accounts or hosting needed for personal use
whatYouLose: Polished card art, flip animations and the deliberate pacing that sells the ritual
Mobile-friendly design someone actually tuned, instead of whatever the agent emits
Multi-language support if you read tarot in anything other than English
Curated spread library and consistent reader persona across sessions
Someone else paying the inference bill
moatNotes: The product is atmosphere. The card logic is trivial; convincing someone the answer means something is the hard part, and that lives in the design, not the code.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a tarot reading is an experience, not a data retrieval, and experiences are mostly tone. People pay for the dim palette, the slow reveal, the sense that a thing was consulted rather than queried. A personal build gives you the same cards and roughly the same words from the same underlying model, but it will look like a dev tool, and for this category looking like a dev tool is fatal to the point. If you want the output rather than the ambience, build it. If you want to feel something, the polish is the product.
notes: Rare case where the code is a Tuesday afternoon and the art direction is the whole business.
prompt:
Build a local-only tarot reading web app. Stack: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3 for saved readings. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data:
- Seed a JSON file with all 78 Rider-Waite-Smith cards: name, arcana, suit, number, keywords for upright and reversed, and an image filename.
- Put card images in /public/cards. Write a script scripts/fetch-cards.ts that downloads the public domain RWS scans from Wikimedia Commons into that folder and skips any that already exist. If a download fails, fall back to rendering the card name on a plain panel.

Core loop:
- Home screen: a text input for the querent's question, a spread picker (Single Card, Three Card past/present/future, Celtic Cross, Horseshoe), and a Draw button.
- Shuffle with crypto.randomUUID-seeded Fisher-Yates, draw without replacement, 30 percent chance each card is reversed.
- Deal the cards face down into a CSS grid laid out per spread, then flip them one at a time with a 400ms stagger using CSS transforms. Celtic Cross gets its proper cross-plus-staff layout, not a grid dump.
- After the flip, POST the question, spread name, and the drawn cards with position labels and orientations to /api/reading.

Reading:
- /api/reading calls the Anthropic Messages API with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env.local and streams the response back.
- System prompt: a tarot reader who interprets each card in the context of its position and the question, then gives a short synthesis. No medical, legal, or financial advice. No hedging disclaimers in the body text.
- Stream the text into the page under the spread so it appears to be written live.

Persistence:
- Save every reading to SQLite: timestamp, question, spread, cards with orientations, full reading text.
- A /history page listing past readings, newest first, each expandable to show the spread and text.

Styling: dark background, serif body type, one accent color, generous whitespace. Restrained, not neon.

Out of scope: user accounts, payments, sharing links, multi-language, daily card notifications, native apps.

Include a README with setup, the card-fetch script, and a .env.example containing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Never commit the real key.
